bullets.title: Iran deal distant despite ceasefire rhetoric; Treasury yields as deal trigger
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side notes converge on the view that Iran-US diplomatic progress is stalling despite Trump's 37 repeated 'imminent deal' declarations. Wolfe sees a distant MOU amid unresolved nuclear, sanctions, and asset-freeze issues, while JPMorgan models a 'base case' shallow deal and flags 10-year yields above 4.5% as the most likely pressure-point to force Trump's hand. Iran clarified it makes no commitment on Hormuz management, and Iran's IRNA says the strait will not return to pre-war status. Latest development: a signed MOU including 60-day ceasefire, Hormuz reopening, oil sanctions relief, and $24B in funds was reportedly nearing completion by G7, with potential Geneva signing—but Iran's foreign ministry called the text 'subject to final decision.' Markets rallied on deal optimism (S&P +0.6%, oil -6.7%) but risk remains elevated.

bullets.title: May CPI in-line at 4.2% YoY; core softer than expected at +0.2% MoM
bullets.body: May headline CPI rose 0.47% MoM (4.2% YoY), in line with consensus, while core CPI came in at 0.21% MoM vs. 0.3% expected—the softest core reading in months. Energy accounted for over 60% of the monthly gain, with gasoline +40.5% YoY. Multiple banks revised core PCE estimates higher post-PPI, with JPMorgan tracking 0.304% and Morgan Stanley at 0.36% for May PCE, but the in-line result was still interpreted positively. JPMorgan calls May CPI the 'high-water mark' and expects Fed to hold through 2026, while Citi forecasts 2-4 hikes starting late 2026/early 2027.

bullets.title: May PPI beats headline on energy; core PCE likely hotter than CPI implied
bullets.body: May PPI came in at +1.1% MoM (6.5% YoY) vs +0.7% consensus—a major headline beat—driven by final demand goods +2.8% MoM, the largest monthly increase on record. Core PPI was softer at +0.4% vs +0.5% est. Portfolio management fees surged +4.8% MoM and airfares +10.6% MoM, widening the CPI-PCE wedge. Morgan Stanley revised core PCE to 0.36% MoM from 0.26% prior; JPMorgan tracking 0.304%. Multiple strategists now expect Fed to remove easing bias at June FOMC and signal 2026 hikes.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bps to 2.25%—first hike since 2023—flags further tightening risk
bullets.body: The ECB delivered a unanimous 25bp hike to 2.25%, its first since 2023, citing rising inflation forecasts (core raised to 2.5% for 2026-27) and indirect energy price pass-through. President Lagarde emphasized no pre-set rate path, but staff projections are consistent with three-four total hikes—JPMorgan forecasts one more in September while acknowledging upside risk. GDP was cut to 0.8% for 2026. ECB officials also flagged July as 'live' pending Hormuz data. BoC held rates at 2.25% but warned that persistent energy inflation could require consecutive hikes.

bullets.title: Fed neutral stance expected at June FOMC; dot plot to show hike risks in 2H26
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Goldman converge on June FOMC holding rates at 3.50-3.75% while removing the easing bias and revising core PCE forecasts up from 2.7% to 3.1%+. Chair Warsh expected to emphasize AI productivity upside but acknowledge inflation persistence. Two to three FOMC members may project 50-75bp of tightening later in 2026. Market pricing has shifted from 17bps of cuts to pricing potential hikes by year-end, with 50% probability of a 2026 hike. Long-run neutral rate recognition is moving up as economy shows less rate sensitivity.

bullets.title: Tech selloff of ~10% from June 2 highs driven by CPO/800V delays, positioning, and AI capex concerns
bullets.body: The S&P tech sector fell ~10% from its June 2 all-time high driven by: (1) SemiAnalysis report citing CPO/800V DC delays to 2028-29; (2) Oracle's heavy capex disclosure ($70B net FY27) with flat EPS guide; (3) ADBE organic ARR guide-down and CFO departure; (4) SMCI's $7B equity raise; and (5) rising real rates pressuring AI infrastructure multiples. JPMorgan tracked retail ETF selling at all-time highs in SOXL, SMH, IGV. Counterargument: multiple sell-side teams (MS, JPMorgan, Lumentum CEO) pushed back on CPO delay narrative, and GS notes AI capex consensus likely too conservative at $920B 2027 vs. realistic $1.1-1.4T.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +0.6% weekly; small-caps outperform (+4% IWM), rotation into non-AI cyclicals
bullets.body: For the week ending June 12, IWM gained 4.0% and now leads NDX YTD (+19.0% vs +17.4%). Mega-cap tech saw worst underperformance vs NDX since 2022 as capital rotated to fund SpaceX IPO and broader de-risking. Semiconductors (SOX +10% intra-week) rebounded sharply as CPO delay concerns were disputed. Software sector fell 5.3% (IGV down 9 sessions). 10-year yields fell below 4.5%, VIX melted to 17 and term structure un-inverted. GS prime data shows Info Tech net sold at fastest 2-month pace; macro products net bought at fastest pace in 2 months. Preferred broadening trade: S&P ex-AI and cyclicals.

bullets.title: Oracle FQ4 beats on RPO (+362% YoY to $638B) but FY27 capex of $70B net sparks selloff
bullets.body: Oracle reported FQ4 EPS $2.11 vs $1.97 est. with RPO surging to $638B (+362% YoY, +$85B q/q), including $75B in BYOH/prepaid contracts. However, the company guides net cash capex of ~$70B in FY27 and plans to raise $40B in debt/equity, with gross margins expected to decline. Stock fell 8-10% as investor focus shifted to FCF dilution. Most sell-side maintained Buy/Overweight; Citi PT $330, UBS $285, Wolfe raised to $225. FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at $90B with 31% CAGR through 2030.

bullets.title: Adobe beats but organic ARR guide-down and CFO departure trigger sharp selloff
bullets.body: Adobe reported FQ2 EPS $5.96 vs $5.82 est. on strong AI-first ARR growth (3x YoY to $500M+), but organic ARR guidance was cut ~$480-500M via freemium strategy pivot. CFO Dan Durn announced departure to Marvell; company still searching for CEO. Stock fell 7-10% as sell-side cut PTs by an average 11% to $284. Multiple downgrades issued (Evercore to In-Line $225, Stifel to Hold $200, Wolfe to Peer Perform). Citi maintains Neutral at $228, UBS at $225. AI-first ARR represents <2% of total ARR, raising concerns about the pace of monetization.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO priced at $135/share; $75B raise, reportedly 4x oversubscribed, opens at ~$138
bullets.body: SpaceX listed on Nasdaq (ticker SPCX) at $135/share for a $75B raise implying ~$1.75-1.8T valuation, reportedly 4x oversubscribed with BlackRock ordering $5B+. Polymarket priced 62% odds of 20%+ first-day gain. SpaceX told investors it aims to test AI data centers in space in 2027. Multiple sell-side initiated: Wolfe Outperform $175 PT (Starship reusability as key thesis); Oppenheimer Outperform $190 PT. Morningstar warned fair value at $63/share. The IPO absorbed significant retail capital, with reports of semi/AI ETF selling to fund allocation. SpaceX planned 20%+ retail allocation.

bullets.title: GS: AI capex consensus too conservative; hyperscaler spending could reach $1.1-1.4T in 2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flags that consensus 2027 hyperscaler capex estimates of ~$920B imply an implausible slowdown (84% to 22% growth), which the firm views as too conservative. GS base case is ~$1.1T (45% growth) and upside ~$1.4T (89% growth). The $35B Broadcom/Apollo/Blackstone AI XPV platform for Anthropic/OpenAI chip capacity, NVDA-OpenAI 10GW Ohio data center lease, and Amazon's $17.5B term loan all support the bullish capex thesis. Data center supply deficit in North America was 12GW in 2025, and Jefferies models a 19GW chip-implied demand vs. only 10.3GW new supply in 2026.

bullets.title: JPMorgan 2H26 outlook: AI supercycle dominant; crowding risks warrant short-term caution
bullets.body: JPMorgan's 2H26 outlook is bullish on AI, large-cap tech, and semis with a 5-year visibility capex cycle, but flags crowding risks for flash crashes. Fed expected on hold through 2026 with risks skewed to hikes in 4Q26/1H27; ECB, BoE, and BoJ all expected to hike in controlled fashion. Upside scenario requires Hormuz reopening + early AI productivity gains; downside from prolonged Hormuz closure triggering oil spike and recession. Bear flattening of US curve expected. EM equities seen as beta to AI narrative; prefer HY over HG in credit.

bullets.title: Leveraged ETFs now $300B+ AUM; SOXL alone drove $12B rebalancing demand—market structure risk
bullets.body: Leveraged ETFs exceed $300B AUM with ~$750B in underlying equity exposure. MS QDS estimates levered ETF short gamma at $15B per 1% SPX move, down 4% WoW but still >99th percentile. A -20% drawdown can generate >2x the selling vs a -10% move. Semiconductors are the most exposed with $100B+ in levered exposure and the largest aggregate short gamma globally. SOXL alone generated ~$12B in net rebalancing demand in recent sessions, equal to ~45% of its prior AUM. Retail demand at $25.5B for the week, only 39th percentile. The VIX spiked from 9 to 21+ and then back to 17 within the digest window.

bullets.title: US labor market solid but ADP weekly payrolls and jobless claims show modest softening
bullets.body: Jobless claims for week of 6/6 came in at 229K vs 220K expected, the highest since February, though residual seasonality was cited (Minnesota, Oregon). ADP weekly payrolls averaged +29K vs +35.8K prior week. Atlanta Fed GDPNow for 2Q revised to +3.3% SAAR. Three-month nonfarm payroll average surged to 188K in May, the largest increase since March 2024. Small business NFIB optimism fell to 95.3 vs 96.0 est., lowest since October 2024. Real wages turned negative for the second consecutive month as 4.2% CPI outpaced 3.4% wage growth.

bullets.title: Bank of Japan Governor hospitalized; June meeting uncertain; rate hike to 1.0% expected
bullets.body: BOJ Governor Ueda was hospitalized and will miss the June monetary policy meeting. Nikkei reports the BOJ may discuss ending quarterly bond-buying reductions and is likely to hike to 1.0% at the June meeting. PSC Macro noted the BOJ is the most behind the curve of DM central banks given policy-growth disconnect and yen weakness. 40-year JGB yields remain near 3.8-3.9%. Japanese wholesale inflation hit 6.3% YoY in May, highest since March 2023. Samsung and SK Hynix's heavy weighting in KOSPI (~50% combined) contributed to that index's extreme volatility (+8.2% in one session, -4.5% in another).

bullets.title: Memory supercycle extends: HBM4 shortages, CSP 2028 LTA bookings, MU FY27 EPS raised to $124-135
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm CSPs have locked up 2027 memory capacity and are now proactively securing 2028 supply ahead of schedule. MU FY27 EPS raised to $124-135 (Wolfe/Citi) vs. consensus $107-115 on 35-40% DRAM/NAND price increases in 2026 and a projected 40% HBM pricing increase in 2027. AMD warns DDR5 won't normalize until 2028. SK Hynix confirmed by Jensen Huang as certified on HBM4 for Rubin, and plans to triple wafer capacity by 2034. Memory shortage now crowding out standard/PC memory with 60-70% displacement. JPMorgan raised STX PT to $920 and WDC PT to $650.

bullets.title: Nasdaq-100 adds ALAB, CRWV, NBIS effective June 22; CHTR removed
bullets.body: Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance effective June 22 adds Astera Labs (ALAB), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Nebius Group (NBIS), while removing Charter Communications (CHTR). The rebalance is estimated at $28.84B gross NASDAQ turnover. CRWV, ALAB, and NBIS all gained 4-5% on announcement in premarket. Separately, the S&P 500 is also rebalancing June 18 close with $49.6B estimated turnover.

bullets.title: Meta faces EU order to open WhatsApp to rival AI chatbots free; also faces social media addiction liability
bullets.body: The EU ordered Meta to provide rival AI chatbots unrestricted access to WhatsApp at no cost within five days, a mandate Meta plans to challenge as 'excessive regulation funded by European companies.' Separately, a Los Angeles Superior Court denied Meta's and Google's motion for a new trial in a youth social media addiction case, upholding $6M in damages (70% Meta, 30% Google). Thousands of additional cases remain pending. Meta's Manus acquisition was also unwound after China's NDRC blocked it.

bullets.title: US net equity supply turns positive for first time since 2021; BofA Bull & Bear indicator at sell signal
bullets.body: Jefferies notes US net equity supply has flipped positive at +$124B annualized, the first time since 2021, as record IPO activity (SpaceX, OpenAI confident filing, Anthropic ~$1T target) and SMCI's $7B equity raise are offset partially by buybacks. BofA Bull & Bear Indicator has reached 8.8, in sell signal territory—historically preceding 2-3% pullbacks though occasionally 15-20% declines. AAII bearish sentiment hit 47.7% (highest since April), bullish at 30.4% (lowest since September 2025). GS/JPM note Mag7 saw -2.3z selling on long side during the correction.
